transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I guess what finally made me come in is that I just don’t feel like myself anymore. I used to make time for things I really enjoyed—painting, hiking, choir, seeing my family on Sundays—and now even if I have a free hour, I just kind of sit there. I can’t seem to care about any of it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yes. Most days I feel really down… like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. I can be in the classroom with students or sitting at home with my husband, and I still feel hollow, like I’m close to crying.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been about eight months, I think. It started building after I took over the STEM-Arts curriculum initiative at work, and it just hasn’t really let up since then.
Do you feel your low mood is mainly a reaction to the stress of taking over that curriculum initiative at work?
I’m not really sure. The work thing definitely added a lot of stress, but it doesn’t feel like just a reaction to that anymore. It kind of spread into everything, if that makes sense.
Before these past eight months, had you been feeling down most days for two years or more?
No, not for two years. This has really been going on for about eight months, since I took over that STEM-Arts curriculum project.
Before this started eight months ago, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of another time like this before, at least not where it was most of the day nearly every day for a couple weeks.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things?
I don’t think so. I mean, I do worry sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed it being excessive or about lots of different things.
Do these feelings seem stronger than you would expect from the stress at work?
I’m not really sure. Work has been a lot, so it’s hard for me to tell if my reaction is more than what would make sense.
Have you noticed a change in your sleep?

Yes. My sleep has been really inconsistent for months. I’ll lie there awake going over grant details in my head, and then I often wake up around three or four in the morning. Even if I manage to sleep longer, I still wake up feeling like I didn’t really rest.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear change in my appetite. It seems kind of normal, I guess.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy?
I’m not sure. I mean, I get tired like anyone does, but I haven’t really noticed it being unusually bad or different in a clear way.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed a clear problem with concentrating. Maybe I get distracted sometimes, but nothing that stands out to me.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty a lot lately?

Yes... I have. Mostly when something goes wrong with the curriculum project, even small things. I start feeling like I’m letting the students down, and then I think about how hard my parents worked so I could have opportunities like this, and I feel like I’m wasting that.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Yes. I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself, but on late nights in the studio I sometimes think it would be a relief if I just didn’t wake up. That scares me. I told my husband because I felt like I couldn’t keep handling those thoughts by myself.
Even when something good happens or you’re away from work, are you still unable to enjoy things?

Yes. That’s actually part of why I came in. Even when I’m not at work, I don’t really enjoy things the way I used to. I used to paint, go hiking, sing in choir, go to Sunday family gatherings… and now if I have a free hour, I just kind of sit there. I can’t make myself care about any of it, and it doesn’t feel like me.
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to function at work or at home?

Yes. It’s been affecting both. I’ve missed several teaching sessions, and I’ve been avoiding student workshops because I just can’t keep up with the responsibilities like I used to.

At home, my husband has had to step in more. I withdraw from family plans, and lately I don’t feel safe just trying to push through it by myself.
If the curriculum project were no longer a problem, do you think you would still feel this depressed?

Yes, I think I would. The project has definitely made things worse, but it doesn’t feel like it’s only that. Most days it’s like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. I can be in a classroom full of students, or at home with my husband, and still feel hollow and close to tears.
